title: export/sync rewrite allowed-signers and revocation files as 0600
description:
git-vouch:2186-2197 _write_atomic uses tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile (mkstemp, mode 0600) then os.replace, so every export/sync leaves gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile and gpg.ssh.revocationFile at 0600, replacing whatever mode the file had. Reproduced on the HEAD snapshot: a 0644 file becomes 0600 after _write_atomic.

Why it matters: these files are public data meant to be read by git. docs/flag-day.md:53 has release tooling switching to exported files; any setup where the exporter and the verifier are different users (service account exporting for a CI or release user, root exporting to a shared path) loses read access after the first export, and git verify-commit fails for everyone else. It fails closed, but silently re-breaks after an admin chmods it back. It is also inconsistent with _replace_at (git-vouch:2761), which creates at 0o666 & ~umask.

Fix: keep the existing file's mode (os.fstat of the target if it exists, else 0o666 & ~umask) and fchmod the temp fd before os.replace; or create the temp with os.open(..., 0o666) like _replace_at.
notes: Fixed (unit core-misc, uncommitted): _write_atomic creates the temp with os.open 0o666 (umask applies) and fchmods it to the existing file's mode. Tests: test_export.py::test_export_keeps_the_mode_of_existing_files, ::test_export_creates_new_files_world_readable.
close_reason: _write_atomic keeps an existing file's mode, else creates 0o666 minus umask; tests test_export_keeps_the_mode_of_existing_files, test_export_creates_new_files_world_readable
